matchups.task: Build a working monthly budget spreadsheet for a $4,200/month take-home income with formula-driven categories, totals, and a leftover/savings calculation
matchups.why: Excel/Sheets-native AI assistants are now core to Copilot Cowork and Gemini's Workspace push this year, so a real formula-driven spreadsheet is a natural stress test

matchups.task: Create a 6-slide investor pitch deck (.pptx) for a fictional eco-friendly meal-kit startup, given the same one-paragraph brief
matchups.why: Slide generation is now table stakes across assistants, but nobody's checked whether the actual .pptx files hold up outside the chat preview

matchups.task: Write a Python script that sorts a messy folder of mixed files into subfolders by file type and modified date, then run it against a real sample folder
matchups.why: OpenCode has surged to 120k GitHub stars this year and is now a real contender against the incumbent coding agents on a task with a checkable, runnable output

matchups.task: Draft a one-page freelance web-design service contract plus a matching one-page invoice (.docx) for a $3,000 project
matchups.why: Freelancers lean on AI for contracts constantly, but a contract is only useful if the actual document is complete and internally consistent, not just plausible-sounding chat text

matchups.task: Write and produce a 60-second product-explainer voiceover (script plus a generated audio file) for a fictional app launch, from the same brief
matchups.why: Voice/audio generation is the newest frontier these assistants are racing on, and it's the first FOWL AI test where the deliverable isn't a document at all
